nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (Email, Company, Score). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Normalize Lead Payload
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming lead records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: sales, support + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Delegate 'sales' to Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.notes: Posts a chat message into a Microsoft Teams channel — same role as a Slack notify, for teams standardized on Teams. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Runs a parameterized SQL statement against Postgres — values are bound via queryReplacement, not string-interpolated, so it's immune to SQL injection. nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per lead (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Log applications: Notion & PostgreSQL

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers capture-forms work end to end across Notion, PostgreSQL, Microsoft Teams, Slack and Google Sheets.

It moves through 26 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Lead Form Submission
2. Normalize Lead Payload
3. Route by Work Type
4. Delegate 'sales' to Sub-workflow
5. Fast-Track 'support' + Alert
6. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
7. Merge Routed Work
8. Fingerprint for Idempotency
9. Drop Already-Processed Items
10. Load Previous Snapshot
11. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
12. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
13. Record Sub-workflow Result
14. Enrich with Reference Data
15. Fold In Enrichment Fields
16. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
17. Archive Row Snapshot
18. Stamp Completion Time
19. Persist Run Metadata
20. Align Field Names
21. Tag Pipeline Metadata
22. Cap Batch Volume
23. Save Execution Metadata
24. Summarize Run Stats
25. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
26. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing capture-forms work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Lead Form Submission → Normalize Lead Payload → Route by Work Type → Delegate 'sales' to Sub-workflow → Fast-Track 'support' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Align Field Names → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Notion and PostgreSQL aligned by hand for capture forms
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Notion, for capture forms
- Capture forms work where "Normalize Lead Payload" is still a manual step before Notion
- Capture forms work that only reaches Notion when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Notion and PostgreSQL in step for capture forms, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Notion or PostgreSQL are skipped, across all 29 nodes of this capture-forms build
- A failed Notion or PostgreSQL call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 29 nodes in this capture-forms build
- Branches rejoin before Notion, so a capture-forms run reports once rather than 29 times
- Every capture-forms run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Notion

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your capture forms process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
capture-forms payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
